$description: Health OS design system tokens. THE single source of truth. Edit this file, then run `npm run tokens` to regenerate tokens.css, tailwind.preset.js and src/lib/palette.ts. Never edit the generated files by hand; `npm run build` fails if they drift.

color.$description: Every colour stops at its full strength and has two lighter shades. There are no darker shades. Apricot is the one interactive accent: apricot-200 fills every button, check, selected state and link underline, and apricot-50 with an apricot-200 edge marks what is selected. Focus rings are ink-900, so where you are never looks like what you chose. Apricot is never decoration, with one exception: the one descriptive word of a headline is apricot-400. Rose, lavender and the ink neutrals carry categories, charts, tiles and the gradients. Widgets and cards use only the two lighter shades, and every other piece of text stays in the ink neutrals.

rose.$description: Expressive Rose, the primary brand colour. Categories, chart data and the middle of the signature gradient. Not an interactive accent: that is apricot.

50.$description: Soft. Tinted fills for rose categories: badges, tile ends and quiet panels.

200.$description: Light. Rose categories in widgets and cards: bars, rings, tiles, chart data, icons and borders on rose tints.

400.$description: Full strength, the primary. Gradient stops and category dots only. Not for text, buttons, focus rings, checked or selected states, widgets or card colour.

apricot.$description: Sunlit Apricot, the warm brand colour and the one interactive accent. The warm start of the signature gradient.

50.$description: Soft. Selected rows, chips and segments (with an apricot-200 edge) and the active navigation item. Not a decorative fill.

200.$description: Light. The accent: every button and icon button fill with ink text, checked checkboxes, radios and switches, selected states, the current step, tab and link underlines, the text selection and the FAQ plus. Also one of the three data colours inside widgets and the celebration confetti. Not for text, decorative cells, badges or icon tiles.

400.$description: Full strength, Sunlit Apricot. The one descriptive word of every headline (the only apricot text in the system), the / in command chips and category dots. Also a gradient stop. Not for focus rings (ink-900), fills, other text, widgets or card colour.

lavender.$description: Neutral Lavender, the cool brand colour. Categories, chart data and the cool end of the signature gradient. Not an interactive accent.

200.$description: Light. The colour of widgets and cards: bars, rings, tiles, chart data, icons and borders on cool fills.

400.$description: Full strength. Gradient stops and category dots only. Not for text, widgets or card colour.

ink.$description: Warm neutrals. The same in both themes.

400.$description: Placeholder text, disabled text, hover borders and muted icons.

500.$description: Secondary text, labels and metadata. The lightest neutral for readable text: at least 4.5:1 on every ground in both themes, including the textured and tinted 50 grounds (darkened from #7C746B on 15 September 2026 after the audit found 12px labels at 3.9 to 4.3:1).

900.$description: Headings, primary text, every word of a headline except its accent word, and every focus ring and focused field border.

carbon.$description: Never a page, panel or card background. Only a translucent veil: the video control bar (carbon/60, carbon/80), the floating video controls and the modal backdrop (carbon/40). The one small dark surface in the system is the icon tile, with its own warm charcoal ground (icon.ground).

white.$description: Icons and text on the video control bar. Never a hand-coded page ground.

success.$description: Functional: confirmations and healthy states. Full strength at 600 and two lighter shades, like the brand colours.

300.$description: Light. Borders on success tints and chart tracks.

600.$description: Full strength. Icons, dots, solid marks.

warning.$description: Functional: needs attention soon. Full strength at 600 and two lighter shades, like the brand colours.

300.$description: Light. Borders on warning tints and chart tracks.

600.$description: Full strength. Icons, dots, solid marks.

error.$description: Functional: something failed or is blocked. Full strength at 600 and two lighter shades, like the brand colours.

300.$description: Light. Borders on error tints and chart tracks.

600.$description: Full strength. Icons, dots, solid marks, and error messages.

theme.$description: Two themes. They share every colour, component and behaviour; only the grounds change. Light is the default; paper adds a warm reading-paper ground.

surface-2.$description: Recessed wells, table headers, input backgrounds.
Recessed wells, table headers, input backgrounds.

brand-gradient.$description: Signature. Apricot to rose to lavender, never reversed. The logo, a highlight behind one headline word, thin accents such as a progress fill. Never a large fill for a card, panel or banner.

brand-gradient-soft.$description: Soft wash. Large quiet fills: section panels, media placeholders, highlight bars and the one scrolling banner. Dark text on top.

brand-gradient-dawn.$description: Soft dawn. A gentle warm light from white into apricot and rose tints. Action cards and invitations, with dark text and the primary button on top.

sans.$description: Body and labels. Anonymous Pro is monospaced: this is the Health OS texture.

heading.$description: One heading size, fluid from 36px on phones to 58px on desktop. Page and section titles, hero headlines, big figures.

subheading.$description: Fluid from 20px to 24px. Card titles, group titles inside a section, compact figures.

title.$description: 18px / 27px medium. Quiet titles in a list of rows: FAQ questions, disclosure rows, settings and step rows. Gentler than a subheading, so a list of questions reads as a list, not a stack of headings.

body.$description: 16px / 26px. All running text, descriptions, inputs, table cells, button labels (in the display family).

label.$description: 12px / 16px bold. Only where needed: badges, eyebrows (uppercase), metadata, table headers, chart axes.

headline.$description: Every H1 is written in ink-900 except one descriptive word (calm, together, make, bookings), which is apricot-400. One to three icon tiles sit beside the words they picture; the accent word does not need a tile of its own. Tiles come from the icon library, stay on the same line as the word before them and do not react to the pointer. Values are in em so tiles scale with the heading.

ink.$description: ink-900 (text-ink-900). Every word of the headline except the accent word.

accent.$description: apricot-400 (text-apricot-400). The one descriptive word, marked [word] in the copy. Heading size only: at about 2.1:1 on white it is a brand moment, not a readable colour for smaller type.

tile-size.$description: Width and height of an icon tile inside a headline, just under the heading size so it sits inside the line.

tile-offset.$description: Vertical alignment that centres a tile on the letters.

tiles-min.$description: The fewest tiles in a headline.

tiles-max.$description: The most tiles in a headline.

tile-tilt.$description: How far each tile is turned. The first tile leans left, the next right and so on, at full, two thirds and five sixths of this value, so tiles float between the words instead of sitting in a row.

float-distance.$description: How far a tile drifts up and down as it floats: about 3px at heading size. Enough to feel weightless, never enough to pull the eye off the words.

float-duration.$description: One slow float, up and back. Tiles start at staggered points so they never move in step. The float stops while the headline is off screen and when reduced motion is on.

leading-stacked.$description: Line height for a headline written on two lines with a line break, such as the home hero: more air between the lines than the heading role's 1.08.

fade-to.$description: Where a fading headline ends: each line runs from ink-900 at the top of the letters to this softer ink at their foot (about 6:1 on white). The home hero only; the accent word stays solid apricot.

logo-height.$description: Height of the long logo when it stands in for the words Health OS inside a headline.

logo-offset.$description: Vertical alignment that seats the long logo on the headline's baseline.

icon.$description: Icon tiles: one photoreal object on a squircle. The same tiles picture words in headlines and stand on their own in cards, bentos, lists and social posts. Three grounds: warm charcoal (the default, and the only dark surface in the system), paper and white for light contexts. One ground per component; tiles stay small.

ground.$description: The warm charcoal ground, lighter at the centre where the object sits. Sampled from Tumai's tiles.

ground-paper.$description: The paper ground: warm ivory, lighter at the centre. For light contexts where a dark square would be the heaviest thing: beside or over photos that dissolve (image fades, vignettes), on tabs and on white surfaces that want warmth.

ground-white.$description: The white ground: plain white. For brand washes, 50 tints and gradient tiles, where it reads as a clean card on the colour.

edge-light.$description: The hairline inside a paper or white tile, so it holds its shape on a ground of the same colour. The charcoal tile has no edge.

object-shadow-light.$description: A soft contact shadow under the object on a paper or white tile, so white and pale objects (a feather, a cable, a paper plane) still read.

radius.$description: The squircle corner, in proportion to the tile's size.

inset.$description: Space between the tile edge and the object image, so the object fills about two thirds of the tile.

size-xs.$description: 28px. Beside a tab label, the smallest a photoreal object still reads.

size-sm.$description: 40px. Beside a list item or a card title.

size-md.$description: 64px. In a feature card or a bento cell.

size-lg.$description: 96px. On its own: a library, a social post, a lead magnet cover.

size-hero.$description: 64px. A tile floating around the home headline on phones.

size-hero-lg.$description: 80px. A tile floating around the home headline from md up.

float-size-min.$description: The smallest tile in a headline field, in the headline's own em: about 44px at full heading size. Tiles in one field take different sizes between the minimum and maximum, so the field looks scattered rather than set out.

float-size-max.$description: The largest tile in a headline field: about 110px at full heading size.

float-rise.$description: How far a floating tile drifts up and down: 8px either way.

float-drift.$description: How far a floating tile drifts side to side: 6px either way.

float-turn.$description: How far a floating tile rocks as it drifts, either way.

float-duration-min.$description: The quickest float cycle. Each tile picks its own pace between the minimum and maximum, so the field never moves in step.

repel-radius.$description: Pixels. A floating tile moves away from the pointer once it comes this close to its centre.

repel-force.$description: Pixels. How far a tile moves away when the pointer is right on it; less the further away the pointer is.

spring-stiffness.$description: Spring stiffness for the repel and the return, so a tile eases rather than jumps.

spring-damping.$description: Spring damping for the repel and the return.

banner.$description: There is one banner: the scrolling strip on the soft wash. No grey, paper, white or dark banner exists, on either theme.

fill.$description: brand-gradient-soft (bg-brand-gradient-soft), with a hairline top and bottom.

text.$description: ink-900. Statements in the label role, uppercase.

icon.$description: ink-500. The small line icon before each statement.

speed-min.$description: The fastest loop. A banner drifts; it never races.

card3d.$description: The floating card: a picture resting at a slight angle so it reads as lifted off the page, tilting toward the pointer and easing back when it leaves, and turning over on a click to show what is behind it. Built for the featured dashboard; portable to any page, since every value here is a CSS variable. Lifted from the Fitness OS hero card (Tumai, 17 September 2026) and put on Health OS ground: ink lift instead of black, an apricot glow, and the system's own easing.

perspective.$description: Depth of the stage the card sits in. It belongs on the parent, never on the card itself, or the card skews flat instead of turning. Lower is more dramatic, higher is subtler.

tilt.$description: How far the card tilts toward the pointer, either way. Past about 12 degrees a large picture warps and the words inside it stop being readable.

rest-x.$description: The resting tilt from the top, which is what makes the card read as floating when nobody is hovering it. It only applies to the front: turned over, the card squares up to the screen so the back is watched level.

rest-y.$description: The resting turn to the side, the other half of the floating angle.

follow.$description: How quickly the card chases the pointer. Longer reads smoother, shorter reads snappier.

flip.$description: How long the card takes to turn over.

lift.$description: The drop shadow that lifts the card off the page, in ink rather than black.

glow.$description: The light behind the card, apricot-400. The one place the brand colour is a glow; swap the three numbers to move it to another brand.

wall.$description: The testimonial walls. Two ways to show a lot of short quotes without a page of stacked cards: rows that drift sideways, and columns that drift upward. Both keep moving slowly enough to read a card as it passes, both stop on hover, focus and the pause button, and both sit still with reduced motion on. Sizes live here so a wall can be lifted into another page and resized from one place.

card-width.$description: A row card. Wide enough for a two-line quote at body size, narrow enough that three or four are in view at once.

card-width-wide.$description: A column card, which carries a longer quote and more padding.

column-height.$description: How tall a column of quotes stands. About three cards, so the fourth is always arriving.

fade.$description: The soft edge at both ends of a moving row or column, so cards arrive and leave rather than being cut off.

row-speed.$description: Pixels a second, sideways. Slow enough to finish reading a card before it goes.

column-speed.$description: Pixels a second, upward. Slower than the rows, because the column cards carry more words.

video.$description: The floating video. When a playing video scrolls out of view it follows the reader into the bottom right corner, and returns to its place when its space scrolls back in. It never floats while paused, and closing it pauses the video.

pip-width-sm.$description: 208px wide on phones, so it covers little of the page.

pip-inset.$description: 24px from the right and bottom edges from sm up.

pip-threshold.$description: The video floats once less than a quarter of its space is visible.

pip-z.$description: Above page content, below dialogs, toasts and menus.

celebration.$description: Confetti: a small celebration when someone commits to something, such as choosing annual billing, booking, confirming or saving. Curly streamers, short ribbons, stars and dots pop up from the top edge of the control, then drift down and fade. Brand colours at 400 and 200, the one place 400 appears as a fill, because it lasts under two seconds. Once per action, never on load, and off when reduced motion is on.

colours.$description: apricot-400, rose-400, lavender-400, then apricot-200, rose-200 and lavender-200.

pieces.$description: How many pieces in one burst: a mini moment, not a party.

duration.$description: From the pop to the last piece fading.

rise.$description: Roughly how high the tallest pieces pop above the control before they fall.

md.$description: Controls: buttons, inputs, chips, badges, icon wells, small tiles.

lg.$description: Containers: cards, panels, media frames, dialogs.

full.$description: Round things only: avatars, dots, toggles, the theme switch.

sm.$description: Hover lift on cards and interactive tiles.

md.$description: Floating UI: menus, popovers, tooltips, toasts.

space.$description: Base rhythm is 8px (Tailwind 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 24). Compact 4px steps (1, 3, 5) are for icon gaps, label padding and dense controls only. The numbered steps match Tailwind's default spacing, so the preset only adds the hero tokens.

2.$description: 8px. Tight gaps inside a control or list row.

3.$description: 12px. Compact: label padding, small chip gaps.

4.$description: 16px. Gaps between related items; input padding.

8.$description: 32px. Padding on larger panels; gaps between groups.

10.$description: 40px. Space between blocks inside a section.

hero-py.$description: Hero top and bottom padding on phones (112px).

hero-py-lg.$description: Hero top and bottom padding from md up (176px).

hero-gap.$description: Gap between hero blocks: subcopy to action (56px).

hero-gap-sm.$description: Tighter hero gap: title to subcopy, action to chips (32px).

hero-gap-lg.$description: The long pause between a home hero's headline group and its search from md up (192px), so the headline and its floating icons own the top of the hero and the search sits in its lower third.

hero-fade.$description: Height of the soft blend at the foot of a page's opening hero, where its ground dissolves into the section below (288px). No line marks where the fold was.

container-wide.$description: Full-bleed panels such as the footer.

narrow.$description: Condensed blocks that should not fill the page, such as FAQs.

motion.$description: Health OS motion is its own: calm, flowing and on by default. Durations and easings keep it consistent; the motion library itself is open-ended.

step.$description: How long a step or slide holds before content that plays on its own moves on, such as feature steps. Long enough to read one step; always with a pause control.
